skills/toil/elasticsearch.md

Cluster health, the index list, and document search and count on Elasticsearch, through its REST API. Every command reads; none changes anything. Verification level: unit.

Supported versions: The oldest Elasticsearch version toil supports hasn’t been established. toil calls _cluster/health, _cat/indices, _search and _count with an API key sent as an ApiKey header, following Elastic’s current REST API reference. No release has been verified yet.

Credential

An Elasticsearch API key: in Kibana, Stack Management → API keys → Create API key (or Elasticsearch’s own POST /_security/api_key). Copy the encoded value, the base64 string shown once when the key is created. Give it the read index privilege on the indices you’ll search and count, monitor on those you’ll list, and the monitor cluster privilege for cluster health and indices list. toil sends it as Authorization: ApiKey <encoded>. There is no username, password or browser login.

Configuration

KeyEnv varRequiredMeaning
baseUrlTOIL_ELASTICSEARCH_BASE_URLyesElasticsearch root, e.g. https://elasticsearch.imagile.dev (keep any context path). Elasticsearch itself, not Kibana
apiKeyTOIL_ELASTICSEARCH_API_KEYyesThe encoded API key

There’s no CI fallback variable.

Environment variables (CI, or a one-off shell):

export TOIL_ELASTICSEARCH_BASE_URL=https://elasticsearch.imagile.dev
export TOIL_ELASTICSEARCH_API_KEY=<your encoded API key>

Or ~/.toil/config.json:

{
  "version": 2,
  "connections": {
    "es-prod": { "area": "elasticsearch", "baseUrl": "https://elasticsearch.imagile.dev" }
  },
  "defaults": { "elasticsearch": { "connection": "es-prod" } }
}

The key never goes in this file; a plaintext one there is refused with CONFIG_INVALID. Run toil connections add es-prod --area elasticsearch (or toil connections login es-prod for an existing connection) to keep it in the OS credential store, or set TOIL_ELASTICSEARCH_API_KEY.

Sharing the key with Kibana: a Kibana connection can use this connection’s key instead of its own, but only when you pair them on the Kibana side ("apiKeyFrom": "es-prod"). An unpaired Kibana connection never gets it. The one exception is an env fallback the contract specifies: Kibana’s default connection takes TOIL_ELASTICSEARCH_API_KEY when TOIL_KIBANA_API_KEY isn’t set. Either way the key is sent only to that Kibana connection’s own host. See kibana.md.

Commands

  • cluster health: Show cluster health (status, node and shard counts), as Elasticsearch reports it. A red cluster is a successful answer whose status is red.
  • indices list: List indices with health, document count and size (--pattern takes a name or wildcard, comma-separate several). data is { count, indices }, each row the _cat/indices columns index, health, status, docs.count, store.size, pri and rep, every value a string.
  • search: Search one or more indices with Query DSL JSON or a query string. --index is required (comma-separate several; wildcards and aliases work; an empty name or an empty entry between commas is refused, so nothing silently searches every index). --query takes one Query DSL clause as a JSON object, --q a Lucene query string; use one or the other, and with neither every document matches. --sort takes field:order pairs, comma-separated (@timestamp:desc,_score:desc; an entry with no asc or desc sorts ascending). --source is a comma list of fields to return. --size (default 100) and --from (default 0) go to the server as given; past 10,000 hits Elasticsearch refuses from + size (its max_result_window). --timeout-ms (default 30000) is how long toil waits for the answer. search has a 10-minute time limit of its own, so a --timeout-ms up to 600000 is honoured; TOIL_TIMEOUT_MS, when set, overrides that limit. data is { index, took, timedOut, total, totalRelation, hitCount, hits, aggregations }: hits as Elasticsearch sent them, and totalRelation gte when total is only a lower bound.
  • count: Count documents matching a query (--index required, --query or --q as for search). data is { index, count }.

search and count send their query as a POST body. They still only read.

Errors carry Elasticsearch’s own reason, e.g. index_not_found_exception: no such index [nope], or a query parse error under its root cause, so a bad query can be fixed from the message.

toil elasticsearch cluster health
toil elasticsearch indices list --pattern "logs-*"
toil elasticsearch search --index logs-app --q "level:error AND service:api" --sort "@timestamp:desc" --size 20
toil elasticsearch count --index "logs-*" --query '{"term":{"level":"error"}}'

Settings at a glance

  • baseUrl required

    Elasticsearch root, e.g. https://elasticsearch.imagile.dev (keep any context path)

    TOIL_ELASTICSEARCH_BASE_URL

  • apiKey required secret

    API key: the encoded value shown once when the key is created

    TOIL_ELASTICSEARCH_API_KEY

Commands at a glance

  • toil elasticsearchcluster health

    Show cluster health (status, node and shard counts)

    MCP elasticsearch_cluster_health

  • toil elasticsearchindices list

    List indices with health, document count and size

    MCP elasticsearch_indices_list--pattern <pattern>

  • toil elasticsearchsearch

    Search one or more indices with Query DSL JSON or a query string

    MCP elasticsearch_search--index <name>--query <json>--q <query-string>--sort <field:order>--source <fields>--size <n>--from <n>--timeout-ms <ms>

  • toil elasticsearchcount

    Count documents matching a query

    MCP elasticsearch_count--index <name>--query <json>--q <query-string>
